ai.definition: AI-Employee Digital Twins are virtual representations of human employees designed to simulate their behavior, decision-making processes, and interactions. These digital twins are trained using data from the actual employee’s work to perform routine tasks and answer queries.
ai.howItWorks: These systems continuously learn from an employee's communications, decisions, and knowledge base through machine learning algorithms. They can then replicate these behaviors in a virtual environment to assist with tasks or provide support to other employees.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for efficient handling of routine queries and tasks by providing a scalable solution that mimics human expertise without the associated costs and limitations of hiring additional human staff.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training machine learning models using historical data from the employee's work. This requires significant computational resources, including powerful GPUs and large datasets.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes data collection, model development, training, and validation. Data is gathered through various sources such as emails, documents, and interactions with other systems. The models are then trained to mimic the employee’s behavior and decision-making processes.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the initial investment in computational resources, ongoing data collection and maintenance, and continuous model training and updates to ensure accuracy and relevance.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to see increased adoption as organizations seek ways to optimize their operations through automation and digital transformation.
ai.regulation: Current regulations around data privacy and employee monitoring vary by jurisdiction. Organizations must ensure compliance with local laws when implementing AI-Employee Digital Twins.
ai.risks: Risks include potential bias in the training data, privacy concerns related to data collection, and the risk of over-reliance on digital twins leading to a reduction in human expertise.
ai.profitability: Profitability is dependent on the specific use case and industry. While it can reduce operational costs by automating routine tasks, there are initial setup costs that need to be considered.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more advanced natural language processing capabilities, integration with other AI technologies like robotics, and enhanced personalization of digital twins based on individual employee characteristics.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Ongoing operation requires minimal power but depends heavily on the computational resources used for training and updating models.

glossary.def: A virtual representation of a human employee designed to simulate their behavior, decision-making processes, and interactions.
A subset of artificial intelligence that involves training algorithms on data to enable them to perform tasks without explicit programming.

subsystems.name: Data ingestion pipeline
subsystems.role: collects the employee's communications, documents, decisions and outcomes with consent and access controls.
parts: connectors to email, chat and document stores

subsystems.name: Knowledge base and vector store
subsystems.role: organises the expert's knowledge so the model can retrieve relevant facts and past decisions.
parts: knowledge graph of entities and relationships

subsystems.name: Language model core
subsystems.role: provides general language understanding, reasoning and generation.

subsystems.name: Personalisation layer
subsystems.role: adapts the general model to the individual's style, priorities and expertise.

subsystems.name: Agent runtime
subsystems.role: turns queries into actions: retrieving information, drafting replies, calling tools or escalating.
parts: tool interface for calendars, ticketing, databases

subsystems.name: Privacy and security layer
subsystems.role: keeps the twin's data isolated and prevents leaks or impersonation.
parts: encryption at rest and in transit
differential privacy or federated learning techniques

subsystems.name: Feedback and evaluation loop
subsystems.role: continuously improves the twin from corrections and outcomes.

buildSteps.title: Define scope and consent
buildSteps.detail: Decide which tasks the twin will handle, obtain the employee's informed consent, and set rules for what data may be used.

buildSteps.title: Collect and clean data
buildSteps.detail: Gather emails, chat logs, documents and decision records; remove sensitive personal data and redact anything outside the agreed scope.

buildSteps.title: Build a private knowledge base
buildSteps.detail: Convert documents into embeddings and a structured graph, stored in an access-controlled system so retrieval only returns what the user is allowed to see.

buildSteps.title: Adapt a base model
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune or attach lightweight adapters to a pretrained language model using the employee's anonymised data and example interactions.

buildSteps.title: Wrap it in an agent
buildSteps.detail: Add a planner that can break down requests, call tools such as email or ticketing APIs, and hand back to a human when confidence is low.

buildSteps.title: Install guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Enforce access controls, rate limits, impersonation warnings and audit trails so the twin cannot act beyond its authority.

buildSteps.title: Pilot in a sandbox
buildSteps.detail: Run the twin in a limited, monitored setting with human review of every action; collect corrections.

buildSteps.title: Iterate continuously
buildSteps.detail: Use feedback to update the knowledge base and adapters, while monitoring for drift, bias and security incidents.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with fine-tuning or adapters
prerequisites.why: they provide the base language and reasoning ability the twin builds on.
lets the model answer from the employee's own documents without retraining from scratch.
techniques such as federated learning and differential privacy exist in research but are not yet routine for this scale of personal data.
organisations need clear rules for using employee communications; practice lags the technology.
a twin must keep learning new facts without erasing old ones, which current methods handle poorly.
agents can call external systems, but error rates and security risks are still high.

pathway.milestone: general-purpose AI assistants that answer questions from a shared knowledge base
pathway.unlocks: routine query handling for many employees.

pathway.milestone: role-specific assistants trained on department documents and past tickets
pathway.unlocks: faster onboarding and consistent answers in support, legal or engineering.

pathway.milestone: personal digital twins for individual experts, with strict access controls and human review
pathway.unlocks: a way to scale an expert's availability without cloning them without consent.

pathway.milestone: federated twins that collaborate and learn from each other under privacy guarantees
pathway.unlocks: organisational memory that persists through staff turnover.
